test_cases.description: InitSchema creates the jobs table and all four required indexes when called with a valid in-memory SQLite database.
preconditions: An in-memory SQLite *sql.DB is open via modernc.org/sqlite with DSN ':memory:'
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 are set on the connection
The jobs table does not yet exist
test_cases.input: InitSchema(db) where db is a freshly opened in-memory SQLite connection
test_cases.expected: Returns nil; querying sqlite_master confirms the jobs table exists with columns id, type, key, nonce, status, payload, result, error, retry_count, available_at, submitted_by, created_at, updated_at; indexes idx_jobs_nonce, idx_jobs_type_key_status, idx_jobs_status_available_at, idx_jobs_type_created_at all exist
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: err = InitSchema(db); assert err == nil; rows = db.Query("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='jobs'"); assert rows has one row; for each index in [idx_jobs_nonce, idx_jobs_type_key_status, idx_jobs_status_available_at, idx_jobs_type_created_at]: rows = db.Query("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index' AND name=?", index); assert rows has one row

test_cases.description: InitSchema called a second time on a database where the jobs table already exists returns nil without error and leaves existing data intact.
preconditions: An in-memory SQLite *sql.DB is open
InitSchema has already been called once successfully
A job row has been inserted into the jobs table
test_cases.input: InitSchema(db) called a second time on the same db
test_cases.expected: Returns nil; the jobs table still exists; the previously inserted row is still present; no duplicate tables or indexes are created
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: err1 = InitSchema(db); assert err1 == nil; db.Exec("INSERT INTO jobs (id, type, key, nonce, status, ...) VALUES ('j1', 'merge', 'main', 'n1', 'queued', ...)"); err2 = InitSchema(db); assert err2 == nil; count = db.QueryRow("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE id='j1'").Scan(); assert count == 1

test_cases.description: InitSchema creates idx_jobs_nonce as a UNIQUE index, causing a second insert with the same nonce to fail with a unique constraint violation.
preconditions: An in-memory SQLite *sql.DB is open
InitSchema has been called successfully
test_cases.input: Two INSERT statements into jobs with identical nonce values
test_cases.expected: First insert succeeds; second insert returns a SQLite unique constraint error referencing the nonce column
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: InitSchema(db); err1 = db.Exec("INSERT INTO jobs (id, type, key, nonce, status, ...) VALUES ('j1', 'merge', 'k', 'same-nonce', 'queued', ...)"); assert err1 == nil; err2 = db.Exec("INSERT INTO jobs (id, type, key, nonce, status, ...) VALUES ('j2', 'merge', 'k', 'same-nonce', 'queued', ...)"); assert err2 != nil; assert err2 message contains 'UNIQUE' or 'unique'

test_cases.description: When a handler returns a retryable error and retry_count < max_retries, the worker increments retry_count, computes backoff delay, sets status=failed, and stores the error message.

Type 'sync' is registered with RetryPolicy{Base: 2s, Multiplier: 2, Cap: 7200s, MaxRetries: 20}
A job with type='sync', key='r42', status='queued', retry_count=0 exists

A job with type='sync', key='r42', status='queued', retry_count=2 exists (already at max)

test_cases.description: When a handler returns a permanent (non-retryable) error, the worker transitions the job directly to dead_letter without incrementing retry_count.

Type 'merge' is registered

test_cases.description: Backoff delay is computed as min(base * multiplier^retry_count, cap) with retry_count already incremented; first failure produces 4s, second 8s, third 16s with default policy.

test_cases.expected: Returns 4s, 8s, 16s respectively
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: assert computeBackoff(defaultPolicy, 1) == 4*time.Second; assert computeBackoff(defaultPolicy, 2) == 8*time.Second; assert computeBackoff(defaultPolicy, 3) == 16*time.Second; assert computeBackoff(defaultPolicy, 11) == 7200*time.Second // capped

test_cases.description: Per-type retry policy overrides are applied when registered; unspecified fields fall back to defaults.

test_cases.description: When the grace period expires before all workers finish, the queue cancels in-flight handler contexts, logs a WARN per interrupted job, and Wait() returns.
